Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City wvm.dilg.gov.ph DELG optN!ON NO SO 08 2024 MELANIE B. MACABODBOD Federation of Purok President Barangay Buenaflor, Tacurong City Dear Ms. Macabodbod This has reference to your letter dated 26 January 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion and clarifications on whether a Punong Barangay's call for re-election of Purok Officials is warranted and within the bounds of the law. Per the representations, you claim that Punong Barangay Marvin B. Bawe of Barangay Buenaflor, Tacurong City is advocating for the re-election of purok officials within their barangay, purportedly with the objective of eliminating all the opposition within his administration. You then represented that the Federation of Purok Presidents are apprehensive that that the call for a re-election of purok elections may be driven by a desire to consolidate power and stifle opposition, rather than a genuine need for a new leadership. Furthermore, you indicated that members of the aforementioned federation are concerned that the re-election may constitute an abuse of authority, as it could lead to manipulation and control of purok operations in the lack of a legitimate basis for re- election. Hence, the request for legal opinion. At the onset, DILG Opinion No. 55, series of 2022 provides that the term "purok" is not officially considered a local government unit (LGU) under Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). In local parlance, it usually refers to geographical zone or division within a barangay. A purok serves as a means to deliver basic services within a barangay, aimed to strengthen participatory governance and a more efficient public service delivery to grassroots level. 1 Formally established puroks are under the control and supervision of the barangay, particularly the ordinance creating or reorganizing the same.2 In this regard, the operational structure of the purok relative to the election of its leaders shall be governed by either of the following• 1 June 10, 2022 2 Ibid "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

1. Duly enacted ordinance which acknowledges and/or institutionalizes their organizational existence in case of a formally established purok; or 2. The internal rules or procedure/by laws of the respective purok organizations, if any, for informally created purok. In the matter at hand, the attached documents show that the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Tacurong has passed an Ordinance No. 030 — 9th SP entitled "An Ordinance Establishing a Comprehensive Mechanism in the Organization of Purok in the Barangays in the City of Tacurong" which was approved last May 10, 2023. Said ordinance effectively institutionalizes the mechanisms in the organization of puroks in the city. Section 22 of said ordinance specifically provides: "Section 22. Term of Office — The term of office of elected Purok officials shall be three (3) years from the date of their assumption to office following their election. The election of Purok officials after the effectivity of this Ordinance shall be on first Saturday of October 2023 and the succeeding election shall be held on the first Saturday of October every three (3) years thereafter. The elected officials shall assume office after havinq been qualified and shall continue to hold office until their successor shall have been elected and qualified." (Emphasis supplied) From the foregoing, the ordinance effectively limited the tenure of elected purok officials to three years from the date of their assumption of office following election. Said ordinance likewise specifically provided that the elected officials shall keep office until their successor is elected. Logically speaking, the elected purok officials shall continue to hold such office until a new purok official shall have been elected and qualified. Thus, punong barangay should recognize and observe the election process and tenure of purok officials if it was conducted in conformity with the abovementioned ordinance and other applicable laws. Consequently, the Punong Barangay of Barangay Buenaflor cannot simply demand for their re-election as long as the purok officials' election procedure was lawfully followed. Further, Section 253 of the Ordinance No. 030 — 9th SP of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Tacurong specifically provides for the grounds for removal of an elective purok official. Accordingly, an elective purok official can only be removed if one of the foregoing grounds is present, and upon following the processes provided under the aforementioned ordinance. 3 "Section 25. Grounds for Suspension and Removal — An elective purok official shall be suspended Or removed from Office in any Of the following grounds committed while in office: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. Disloyalty to the Republic Of the Philippines Culpable violation Of the constitution Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office and neglect of duty Commission of any offence involving of moral turpitude Abuse of Authority Unauthorized absence for three (3) consecutive meetings in the purok Page 2 of 3

Thus, the calling for re-election of purok officials in barangay Buenaflor is unnecessary because there is an existing ordinance that clearly institutionalizes the mechanisms in the election of purok officials in the city of Tacurong, as well as the grounds and processes for the removal of purok officials. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OFT E SECRETARY. ATTY N CTOR R. LLAMAS secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs O ELLA/JVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm copy furnished: ATTY.
